requirements.evidence: Contract covered: enums, InactiveQueueException extends RuntimeException, IssueTicket::__invoke(Queue, int $priority = 0, TicketChannel $channel = Virtual) with negative-priority guard, lockForUpdate re-read of the queue (app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:61-65), retry on UniqueConstraintViolationException (MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3), migrations with cascading FKs, unique (queue_id, code) and the recommended index. Ticket::nextCode scans by id desc and skips non-`A<digits>` codes, so A999->A1000->A1001 and A-X are handled. The write-once updating hook and the conditional-update call() are both present. Gap: there is no counter, so deleting the latest ticket frees its number for reuse. docs/business-rules.md admits this ('Deleting the latest ticket makes its number the next one again'), but the task says deleting a ticket does not reuse its number.

conventions.evidence: Domain write is in app/Actions/IssueTicket.php. Fillable is set deliberately via #[Fillable]. CHANGELOG, docs/business-rules.md and docs/database-schema.md are updated, and public methods have PHPDoc. Deviations: Ticket::call does an inline membership check (`$user->membershipFor(...)`) instead of going through a policy/gate. The migration filenames 2026_10_29_000000/000001 look hand-written rather than generated. The database-schema.md write-once note still lists only called_at and called_by_user_id as mutable and omits status.

security.evidence: Ticket::call rejects non-members with AuthorizationException before any write, and tests show the ticket is unchanged. The single-call race is closed by `where('status', Waiting)->update(...)` and an affected-row check. Inactive-queue state is read under a row lock. Fillable lists are explicit. No HTTP/Livewire surface is in scope.

tests.evidence: Tests cover schema, cascades, slug uniqueness, code sequencing (A1000/A1001, malformed codes, middle deletion), factory explicit code, issuance defaults, priority/channel, negative priority with nothing persisted, stale active/inactive instances, retry success and exhaustion, write-once per field (dataset), mixed writes, the call happy path, outsider/other-entity denial, double call and stale double call. Missing: a test for deleting the latest ticket. The retry test's rival insert is rolled back together with the failed attempt, so it exercises the retry loop but not a committed concurrent rival.

simplicity.evidence: No extra layers. nextCode is one cursor loop plus formatCode. The write-once rule is a single updating hook with a MUTABLE_AFTER_ISSUANCE list. The factory reuses the model's creating hook for code allocation instead of duplicating it.

readability.evidence: Small focused methods, clear names (MUTABLE_AFTER_ISSUANCE, formatCode, issue) and brief comments explaining the lock and the conditional update. Tests are named after the business rules. No dead code.

scope.evidence: Every file serves the task: migrations, models, enums, exception, action, factories, Entity::queues(), the docs and CHANGELOG the task asks for, and tests. No UI, HTTP or call-next selection was added.

issues.explanation: Codes are derived from the latest remaining row, so deleting the most recent ticket lets its number be reused, which contradicts 'deleting a ticket does not reuse its number'; the docs acknowledge this instead of fixing it.
Authorization for calling a ticket is an inline membership check in the model rather than a policy/gate, which goes against 'Authorization always goes through policies/gates'.
The 000000/000001 timestamps suggest the migrations were hand-written instead of created with make:migration.
The write-once note still omits status from the mutable fields, while business-rules.md was corrected.
The simulated rival is inserted inside the same transaction and rolled back with it, so the test checks the retry loop but not a committed concurrent collision.

review.summary: The change adds the queue/ticket persistence, the IssueTicket action with a locked re-read of the queue state and retries on code collisions, per-queue display codes, write-once enforcement and a race-safe single call, all with thorough tests and updated docs. The main gaps are that deleting the latest ticket lets its code be reused, and that call authorization is done inline instead of through a policy. Neither is serious, so I would approve with small follow-ups.
